The gold matches the 1926.1401 definitions as I know them, but the supplied text cuts off at 'Climbing' and omits the floating crane, land crane and employer-made equipment definitions. Re-attach them and confirm the tool can retrieve them.
The gold implies tag lines are mandatory, but 1407(b)(2) only requires them to be nonconductive if used. The planning meeting and tag line rules are also not in the supplied text.
The gold implies nonconductive tag lines are required even if the transmitter is deenergized. In 1408(f), they are part of the alternative to deenergizing, so a small fix is needed.

The cited exemptions are correct, but 1926.1400(c)(4), not in the given text, excludes digger derricks from Subpart CC for electric or telecom pole work and handling associated pole materials. Whether 1410 applies at all therefore depends on the task, which the question doesn't state.

Correct under 1926.1412(h), but the question doesn't say it's construction work. 1910.180(d) has its own idle-crane rule (inspection after 1 month or more, under 6 months, plus rope checks), which an expert should weigh.
The core matches 1412(g), but the summary of (f)(4)-(6) leaves out the immediate determination and the temporary-measures exception. It also implies every non-hazard deficiency must be monitored.
The counts are right, but 'can't be used until the removal criterion is met' garbles (a)(4)(ii), which requires complying with that criterion, replacing the rope or severing a localized defect.
The limits are correct, but the closing line needs the qualifier that both broken wires are within one rope lay at the end connection.
The 5% threshold is right, but 'can't be used until the removal criterion is met' misstates (a)(4)(ii).

The Category I process is right, but 'Unlike Category II and III, removal is not automatic' is wrong or unsupported: Category II also allows following the manufacturer's criterion, and no Category III text is given.

The text's 'removable horn' wording shows non-built-in horns are contemplated. From memory, not the supplied text, (a)(7)(i) allows a horn that isn't built in if it's on the equipment and immediately available to the operator, so a flat 'No' may be wrong about the air horn. An expert should check (a)(7)(i).

The core answer matches 1431(d)(5), but the last sentence about anti two-block and controlled load lowering isn't supported by the given text and should be removed.

1441(j) bans hoisting personnel only on equipment covered by that section. 'Little 1 ton hoist' doesn't show it is Subpart CC equipment rather than another kind of hoist outside 1441, so an expert should check the ambiguity.

The gold matches 1910.180(e)(2), but the question doesn't say which standard applies.
